newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end up on stronger soybean.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end up on stronger soybean.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher on Monday due to buying from individual investors encouraged by a rise in soybean futures, traders said.
Prices were 130 to 230 yen higher, with the benchmark March 1998 contract up 230 yen at 16,860 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 78,364 lots.

Active buying from local investors emerged, in line with price rallies of soybean market, traders said. The June, the August and the October contract of Tokyo soybean futures had daily 1,200 yen daily limit by the close, as the stronger CBOT overnight trading encouraged investors to buy, they said.
The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.07-3/4 per bushel at 0905 GMT, down from $3.08-1/4 at the previous close.
The spot May of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $8.66 per bushel at 0905 GMT, up from $8.55 at the previous close.
